question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` support `chrome-extension://*`, and what constrained wildcard grammar is acceptable for the Gateway browser-origin boundary?
rationale: This changes which browser origins may reach Control UI/WebChat gateway connections, so automation should not choose the permanent security policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a constrained Chrome-extension wildcard
options.body: Allow only a narrow `chrome-extension://*` scheme pattern with explicit tests and docs, while keeping HTTP(S), host, and protocol wildcards rejected.

options.title: Prefer exact opaque origins only
options.body: Land or adapt an exact-origin custom-scheme fix such as the related exact-origin PRs and leave extension ID churn to operator config or extension packaging.

options.title: Use a separate patterns API
options.body: Require a new constrained `allowedOriginPatterns`-style config surface for wildcard semantics instead of overloading `allowedOrigins`.

recommendation.title: Approve a constrained Chrome-extension wildcard
recommendation.body: Allow only a narrow `chrome-extension://*` scheme pattern with explicit tests and docs, while keeping HTTP(S), host, and protocol wildcards rejected.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest history-backed owner for browser-origin security hardening is the trusted-proxy HTTP origin-check work.
